summary: The harness now requires a versioned Codex Desktop in-app Browser evidence bundle for production verification. Screenshots, raw DOM/state/console, interaction, overflow, accessibility, and component-runtime observations must share one current runtime-tree digest, producer run, browser session, timestamps, and verified artifact hashes. Legacy production-ui-runtime-check/v1 narrative JSON cannot satisfy the new blocking gate.
decisions: production-browser-evidence-bundle/v1 is the only browser evidence contract accepted by the new production gate; the default registered path is build/system/production/browser-evidence-bundle.json.

The bundle requires an explicit codex-desktop-in-app-browser producer, in-app-browser tool, Browser skill, agent run id, and one timestamped browser session. Python validates the resulting files but does not claim to launch or attest the privileged IAB backend.

Every validated screenshot SHA and one aggregate raw observation for DOM, state, console, interaction, overflow, accessibility, and component-runtime must be present. Non-screenshot observations use production-browser-observation/v1 and bind their own producer/session/tree metadata.

The component-runtime browser observation must match the complete component-runtime-manifest/v1 component id and evidence SHA sets and link the session's DOM, state, and interaction observation ids. The existing component_runtime.py validator remains unchanged.

production-ui-runtime-check/v1 may remain as historical aesthetic-report compatibility data, but it is legacy-unverified and cannot satisfy browser_evidence_bundle; a missing bundle therefore fails closed.
production_verifier.py was limited to resolving paths and adding the new blocking browser_evidence_bundle gate; bundle semantics live in visual_evidence.py.

risks: Producer and session metadata are traceability controls, not a cryptographic browser attestation. Release review must still confirm the Production QA agent actually used the IAB tool and inspect its raw observations.

The existing World Cup Hub runtime-check/v1 files were intentionally not rewritten or promoted. They will not satisfy the new browser gate; a fresh real IAB session and bundle are still required after the runtime tree is frozen.
Test fixtures synthesize contract-shaped observations to exercise validator behavior. They demonstrate fail-closed parsing and binding, not evidence that a real application browser session occurred.

Repository-wide validate-agent-team is deferred to Team Lead after the concurrently regenerated World Cup compiler artifacts receive their own current completion handoff; this QA handoff itself validates cleanly.
next_action: Team Lead may now dispatch a project Production QA run after implementation freeze. That agent must use browser:browser against the actual app, capture and register the full v1 bundle, then hand current evidence to the Release Governor for an independent verify-production-ui decision.
